prior_defects.evidence: Head re-derives the module path from classname when the junit file attribute disagrees (`_junit_failed_nodeids` filename re-derivation, ~lines 115-118), and `junit_case_node_id` derives path from classname on mismatch. Covered by [redacted] and [redacted].

`junit_case_node_id` (misses path) still duplicates the junit-to-nodeid mapping in `_junit_failed_nodeids` (build-map path). They diverge: `_junit_failed_nodeids` drops a case when the classname module is absent from disk, while `junit_case_node_id` falls back to `_junit_module_parts`. They also diverge on empty classname (see new defect 1).

defects.title: Empty classname with no file attribute yields unselectable '.py::<name>' node
defects.detail: When classname is '' and the junit case has no file attribute (or repo lookup fails), `junit_case_node_id` calls `_junit_module_parts('')`, which returns ([], []). The path then becomes '/'.join([]) + '.py' = '.py', producing node IDs like '.py::tests.unit.x.test_bad'. These can never match a selected node, so `shadow_misses` reports them as misses and `miss_report` sets would_escalate=true. `_junit_failed_nodeids` skips the same cases (`continue`), so the two paths disagree. Shadow-mode escalation metrics are inflated. Fix: return None for empty classname with no filename and skip the case, matching `_junit_failed_nodeids`.

prior_defects.evidence: scripts/coverage_test_selection.py:113-117 (_junit_failed_nodeids) re-probes the junit classname with _junit_case_filename(repo, "", classname) when the file attribute's module does not match classname, so inherited failures resolve to the defining module's path instead of a file-anchored bogus ID. The misses path (junit_case_node_id, ~1181-1204) falls back to the _junit_module_parts heuristic, which yields the correct ID for pytest-collected modules. tests/unit/scripts/test_coverage_test_selection.py:~325 [redacted] asserts failed_nodes == ["tests/unit/core/test_engine.py::TestSub::test_inherited"]; the repo fixture creates tests/unit/core/test_engine.py.

Two junit-to-node derivations remain. _junit_failed_nodeids (scripts/coverage_test_selection.py:97-126) probes the filesystem for classname mismatches, while junit_case_node_id (~1181-1204) and failed_node_ids (~1206) reimplement the parse loop and use the _junit_module_parts string heuristic (~1174-1179) on mismatch, with no probe. The two paths can disagree for the same testcase, for example when a classname module is not test_*/*_test named. The misses report then compares against IDs that build_map would not produce. Under pytest's default collection patterns the heuristic matches the probe, so the divergence is latent rather than observed.
